title: He didn’t take the throne first.
paragraphs:
He didn’t take the throne first.
He took their hearts.
And that should terrify you.

Because what deceived Israel…
is still deceiving people today.
Here’s the part nobody warns you about:

The most dangerous voices in your life
won’t look like enemies.
They’ll look like answers.

They’ll sound like comfort.
They’ll feel like validation.
They’ll speak directly to your wounds.
And that’s exactly how Absalom won.
He didn’t start a war.
He started a conversation.

At the gate.
In the ordinary places.
In the spaces where people felt ignored.
He listened.
He affirmed.
He sympathized.

But behind the smile…
was a strategy.
“So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.” — 2 Samuel 15:6

Not led.
Not shepherded.
Not discipled.
Stole.
Let that sink in.
Because stolen hearts don’t realize they’ve been taken.
They think they’ve found something.
And here’s where it hits us.
This isn’t just Absalom’s story.
This is ours.

Some of us have followed voices
that made us feel seen…
but slowly pulled us away from truth.

Some of us have believed lies
because they were wrapped in empathy.

Some of us…
if we’re honest…
have been Absalom.
That quiet hunger to be admired.
That subtle craving to be the one people run to.

That hidden desire to gather attention…
instead of pointing people to God.
It doesn’t look evil.
It looks beautiful.
2 Samuel 14:25 says:
“In all Israel there was no one so much to be praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom.”

He had the look.
The presence.
The charisma.

But heaven doesn’t measure influence
the way people do.
Because charisma can gather a crowd…
…but only character can carry a calling.
And here’s the warning:

You can win people
and still lose your soul.
Absalom stole hearts.

But it led to rebellion.
Division.
Destruction.
His story didn’t end in glory.

It ended hanging…
caught between heaven and earth.
(2 Samuel 18:9)
That image is haunting.
Because that’s what pride does.
It lifts you high enough to be seen…

then leaves you suspended
without support.
Now pause.
Let this go deeper.
This isn’t just about false leaders.
It’s about misled hearts.
Why were the people so easily swayed?
Because they were already hurting.
Already disappointed.
Already longing for justice.
And Absalom stepped into that gap.
Not to heal…
…but to hijack.
And this is where the EMOTIONAL TRIGGER hits:
secret sin → grace

Because the most dangerous deception
is the one that agrees with your hidden pain
while quietly disconnecting you from God.
You don’t fall all at once.
You drift.
You stop checking Scripture.
You start trusting feelings.
You stop seeking God’s voice.
You start chasing voices that sound like Him.
And suddenly…

you’re far from truth
but still convinced you’re right.
Proverbs 4:23 says:
“Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.”
Guard it.

Not everything that touches your heart
is sent by God.
Some voices don’t come to heal you.
They come to own you.
But here’s where everything changes.
Here’s where the Gospel steps in.
Because there is another King…
who also wins hearts.
But He does it completely differently.

Jesus Christ
doesn’t steal hearts.
He redeems them.
He doesn’t flatter your wounds.
He tells the truth about your sin.
He doesn’t manipulate your emotions.
He transforms your soul.
He doesn’t build a following through charm.
He builds a Kingdom through the cross.
Romans 5:8 says:
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

While we were deceived.
While we were wandering.
While we were chasing voices that weren’t Him.

Jesus didn’t stand at the gate
trying to win popularity.

He went to the cross
to win redemption.

Absalom said,
“Follow me.”

Jesus says,
“Deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Me.” (Luke 9:23)
Absalom fed pride.
Jesus crucifies it.
Absalom built a movement around himself.
Jesus leads you back to the Father.
And here’s the truth that will set you free:
You don’t need to chase validation.
You need transformation.
You don’t need someone to agree with you.
You need Someone to save you.
And His name is Jesus.
So let me ask you—honestly:
Who has your heart right now?

Is it a voice that comforts you
but never confronts you?

Is it a platform that feeds your feelings
but starves your spirit?

Or is it the King
who loved you enough
to bleed for you?
If you’ve been deceived…
there is grace.
If you’ve been wandering…
there is a way back.
If you’ve been trying to win people…
instead of walking with God…
there is mercy.
Repent.
Not as punishment.
But as return.

Turn from the voices.
Turn from the pride.
Turn from the hidden places.
And come back to Jesus.
Because stolen hearts can still be restored.
And broken hearts can still be redeemed.
